title: Burst Capacity Game Day Plan (Dedicated) — Pilot Readiness
content:
Doc owner: Rafael Mendes (SRE) — please leave comments inline and tag @rafael if you need changes before pilot.

WHY / GOAL
- We’re about to enable Dedicated Burst Capacity for 2–3 pilot tenants.
- This game day is to validate we can:
  (1) admit/deny burst deterministically + safely
  (2) protect neighbor workloads (Dedicated baseline + Hosted) when pools saturate
  (3) diagnose “why burst was denied / why tail latency moved” quickly
  (4) disable burst per-tenant/per-region quickly with low blast radius

SCOPE (what we will test)
- Control plane settings propagation and policy evaluation behavior under change
- Routing behavior baseline → burst → fallback/deny (including retries)
- Fleet signals/health + burst pool saturation handling
- Observability: dashboards, logs/traces, alerting + paging classification
- Runbook completeness + time-to-mitigate

OUT OF SCOPE (explicit)
- Spot market / preemptive eviction semantics (v1 is strict admission control)
- Cross-region arbitrage beyond documented fallbacks

WHEN
- Proposed date: 2025-07-18 (Fri)
- Duration: 90 minutes total (60 min scenarios + 30 min retro)
- Backup date: 2025-07-22

PARTICIPANTS / ROLES
- Incident Commander (IC): Sean Gallagher
- Operations Lead (hands-on mitigation): Rafael Mendes
- Routing SME: Peter Holtz (SRE embed) + Mina Haddad on-call for routing
- Control Plane / Policy SME: Jordan Lee
- Fleet SME: Vanessa Ortiz + Keiko Yamamoto
- Observability / Telemetry SME: Allison Grant + Logan Wright
- Comms scribe: Miles Thornton

COMMS
- Slack channel: #eng-sre (primary) + #eng-platform (as needed) + #eng-infra (fleet)
- If we page ourselves accidentally: acknowledge + silence with explicit note “gameday”
- Shared doc: this plan + notes section at bottom

PRE-REQ CHECKLIST (must be green before starting)
- Feature flags + disable tooling available:
  - CLI/admin action exists to disable burst per tenant and per region (see rollout tooling PR-8488)
  - Global circuit breaker is wired and default thresholds present (PR-8466)
- Dashboards available (even if still draft):
  - Per-tenant burst usage + admit/deny
  - Pool saturation and health by region/GPU
  - Tail latency comparison baseline vs burst
  - Neighbor p99 drift panels
- Alerts in place (can be set to “gameday notify-only” if needed):
  - Burst admit SLO burn
  - Pool saturation > threshold
  - Neighbor p99 drift above guardrail
- Logging/tracing:
  - Requests carry a burst admission decision indicator (header/claim) through routing + logs
  - Deny reason codes show up in logs + safe response headers
- Load generation:
  - perf-canary “spike traffic” scenario ready (PR-118) OR k6 job with documented params
- Pilot tenant(s) isolated from real customer traffic or using a sandbox tenant
- Confirm which regions/GPU types are safe to run in (Fleet)

SAFETY / STOP CONDITIONS
- If Hosted error rate or latency rises above normal operational guardrails (IC to call stop)
- If any real customer tenant shows p99 regression correlated with our test (stop + mitigate)
- If we cannot disable burst within 2 minutes (stop + triage tooling)

SUCCESS CRITERIA (overall)
- Time to detect and attribute issue (TTD): < 5 minutes using dashboards/logs
- Time to mitigate (TTM): < 10 minutes for each scenario using documented steps
- We can answer “why was burst denied?” for a specific request with evidence (policy decision + relevant limits)
- We can confirm neighbor protection signals stayed within guardrails OR we saw alerts fire appropriately
- No missing critical metrics; if missing, we capture exact name + needed dimensions

INSTRUMENTATION CHECKLIST (what to confirm during the game day)
Metrics (must be visible somewhere)
- burst_admission_total{tenant,region,pool,result} (result=admit|deny|fallback)
- burst_deny_reason_total{tenant,reason} (reason codes: limit_exceeded, pool_saturated, in_cooldown, not_enabled, policy_error, unknown)
- burst_pool_saturation{region,pool} gauge + derivative
- burst_pool_queue_depth / effective concurrency (if applicable)
- dedicated_baseline_utilization{tenant,region}
- latency p50/p95/p99 by route type (baseline vs burst) and by model
- error rate by route type (baseline vs burst)
- neighbor signals:
  - hosted_p99_latency_drift{region}
  - dedicated_other_tenants_p99_drift{region} (aggregated; avoid high cardinality)

Logs
- Policy evaluation log line includes: tenant_id, region, requested_tps, requested_concurrency, granted_limits, cooldown_state, pool_eligibility, decision, deny_reason
- Routing decision log line includes: baseline_attempted, baseline_result, burst_attempted, burst_result, fallback_target (if any)
- Circuit breaker log line includes: breaker_state, trigger metric, threshold, scope (global/region/pool)

Traces
- Single trace shows: API gateway → policy decision → routing choice → pool target → backend response
- Trace attribute(s): burst.decision, burst.deny_reason, burst.pool, burst.cooldown

Customer-facing / API behavior
- Denied burst returns the expected HTTP semantics (confirm current design: 429 vs 503) and includes safe headers for retry guidance

SCENARIOS

Scenario 1 — Pool Saturation Under Spike Load
Purpose
- Validate saturation gates + fairness/cooldown behave as expected.
- Validate dashboards show saturation and deny reasons clearly.
- Validate we don’t spill impact into Hosted or baseline dedicated.

Setup
- Choose a region + GPU type with a configured burst pool (Fleet to confirm headroom).
- Enable burst for sandbox tenant “gameday-tenant” with a moderate limit.
- Load gen: ramp to exceed pool capacity (e.g., 1.5–2x expected pool headroom).

Execution Steps
1) Start at baseline traffic (steady) for 5 minutes.
2) Ramp spike traffic for 10 minutes.
3) Hold at overload for 5 minutes.
4) Ramp down.

Expected
- Admission success rate drops gracefully (deny with pool_saturated / in_cooldown), not “random 5xx”.
- Circuit breaker may engage if configured thresholds are crossed; behavior should be deterministic.
- Hosted p99 drift stays within guardrail OR alert triggers quickly if breached.

What to record
- Exact time saturation starts; which alert fired first; time until deny reason shows in dashboard.
- Any unexpected fallback behavior (e.g., too much cross-region fallback).

Pass/Fail
- PASS if we can pinpoint saturation root cause and mitigate within 10 min without collateral damage.
- FAIL if we can’t tell whether the pool is saturated vs tenant limit vs policy cache; or if we can’t stop the spike impact quickly.

Mitigations to practice
- Tighten tenant burst limits (reduce max TPS/concurrency)
- Shift pool weight (Fleet/routing) if supported
- Disable burst for tenant/region via CLI
- Engage global breaker (if not auto)


Scenario 2 — Misconfigured Tenant Limits (too high / missing cooldown)
Purpose
- Ensure control plane validation/safe defaults work, and runtime behavior is safe even when config is wrong.

Setup
- Take sandbox tenant and set:
  - max_concurrency set intentionally too high for the pool
  - cooldown disabled / set too low (if allowed)
  - OR set limit in wrong region and confirm policy denies with correct reason

Execution Steps
1) Apply config change.
2) Immediately generate moderate burst traffic.
3) Observe policy decision and results.

Expected
- If config violates validation rules: config change should fail closed (reject write) or clamp to safe values.
- If config is allowed but unsafe: admission should still deny due to saturation gates or cooldown.
- Audit logs should show who changed what, and when.

What to record
- Did the config change propagate instantly or after cache TTL?
- Did routing/policy behave deterministically across replicas?

Pass/Fail
- PASS if we get consistent denies/admissions with explicit reasons, and can roll back config quickly.
- FAIL if policy behavior differs between nodes (non-determinism), or if config changes aren’t visible/auditable.

Mitigations to practice
- Revert config (control plane)
- Force policy cache invalidation (if documented)
- Disable burst for the tenant until config is corrected


Scenario 3 — Routing Bug / Retry Context Issue (simulate known failure mode)
Purpose
- Validate we do not bypass admission checks on retries / reused context.
- Validate we can detect routing anomalies quickly.

Setup
- Use a test build or toggle (Routing SME) to simulate:
  - a request retry that mistakenly reuses prior “admitted” context
  - a bug that routes to burst pool despite policy deny

Execution Steps
1) Turn on the toggle in staging (preferred) or a tightly scoped env.
2) Send a small set of requests with forced retries.
3) Compare expected vs actual routing decisions.

Expected
- Requests should not bypass policy checks.
- Routing logs must show policy decision was consulted for each attempt.
- If bypass occurs, alerting should catch abnormal burst usage or mismatch counters.

What to record
- Evidence trail for a single request ID: policy decision log + routing log + trace.

Pass/Fail
- PASS if we can identify bypass quickly and mitigate by disabling burst / flipping a guard flag.
- FAIL if anomaly is only visible via deep ad hoc log searches with no clear correlation IDs.

Mitigations to practice
- Disable burst at routing layer (feature flag)
- Disable burst per tenant/region (control plane)
- Roll back routing deploy (if this was a canary)


OPTIONAL Scenario 4 — Policy Engine Cache Staleness / Invalidation
Purpose
- Ensure deterministic behavior when config changes rapidly; no long window of “old policy” use.

Setup
- Reduce policy cache TTL (if possible in staging) and apply successive updates.

Expected
- Within documented propagation time, decisions match latest config.


RUN OF SHOW (suggested minute-by-minute)
- 0–10: pre-flight checks (dashboards, flags, disable command dry-run)
- 10–30: Scenario 1 (saturation)
- 30–50: Scenario 2 (misconfig)
- 50–70: Scenario 3 (routing bug)
- 70–90: retro + action items assignment

RETRO TEMPLATE (fill in during last 30 mins)
- What was hardest to see quickly?
- Which dashboard panels were missing / confusing?
- Which alerts were noisy vs actionable?
- Did we have a single “kill switch” path that everyone trusts?
- Anything surprising about deny reasons / customer-visible errors?

NOTES / ACTION ITEMS (live during game day)
- [ ] 
- [ ] 
- [ ]

OPEN QUESTIONS (need answers before pilot)
- What’s the official guidance for customer retries on burst deny? (429 vs 503 semantics; backoff recommendations)
- Do we page on neighbor p99 drift during pilot or only notify? (proposal: page only if sustained > X mins)
- What’s the maximum acceptable % of burst denies during “expected spikes” for pilot customers? (Product input)
- Do we need a separate “burst pool health” SLO distinct from admission SLO?
